shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures ended higher on Wednesday after a choppy trade and amid a lack of fresh news.

children: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures ended higher on Wednesday after a choppy trade and amid a lack of fresh news.
Canadian farmers will produce 11% less wheat and about the same amount of canola as they did last year, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday in its first crop production report of 2026.
Average protein content in this year's French soft wheat crop reached 11.8%, up from 11.3% last year, farm office FranceAgriMer said on Wednesday.

Confirming previous indications of improved milling quality in the new crop, the office said in a press presentation that average test weights rose to 79.3 kg per hectolitre from 78.6 kg last year, while moisture fell to 11.3% from 12.6%.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture late Monday said planting of the U.S. winter wheat crop for harvest in 2027 was 8% complete, in line with trade expectations but behind the five-year average of 12%.
The U.S. spring wheat harvest was 93% complete, ahead of the five-year average of 92%.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) finished up 2-1/4 cents at $7.30-3/4 a bushel.
K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) ended 3-1/4 cents higher at $7.99-1/2 a bushel and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) rose 7-1/2 cents to $7.56 a bushel.
